newsitem.title: USA: Asian crudes boost foreign pickings on Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes boost foreign pickings on Gulf Coast.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast refiners attracted a host of foreign crudes from across the globe on Wednesday amid feeble margins and spotty demand in Europe and the Far East, traders said.

Aside from the usual North Sea, West African and Latin American offerings, sellers were heard tentatively courting Gulf Coast refiners with Far East grades such as Widuri and Minas from Indonesia, Kutubu from Papua New Guinea and Gippsland from Australia, grades that usually remain around Asia.
"This is a fishing expedition to see if it makes sense to bring (the Asian crude) over here," one market source said.
Traders speculated that the Asian appetite for crude had slowed down.
From the North Sea, Brent was offered at a steady 65 cents under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for July 7-12.
The July spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.50-55 a barrel Wednesday afternoon, steady with late Tuesday but 15-20 cents off last week's level.
European sources indicated that dated Brent was set to plunge, however, after a trading house had kept the price artificially high to support a CFD (contract for differences) position.
From Nigeria, a trading house was offering Bonny Light for third-decade June at dated Brent plus 50-60 cents a barrel.

Closer to home, sweet crudes were already under pressure. Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol awarded a cargo of Cusiana crude oil to a U.S. refiner for loading June 23-24 at a discount of $1.30-40 a barrel to WTI/Cushing, traders said.
The sale marks Ecopetrol's second attempt to sell this cargo. The company last week decided to cancel a tender for the same cargo for loading June 17-18 after failing to receive acceptable bids.
Ecopetrol then shifted the loading dates to June 23-24 in an effort to spur more interest.
The gasoline-rich grade was last sold into the Gulf Coast for a discount of around $1.23 to WTI/Cushing.
The recent softening in part reflects firmer Caribbean freight rates, traders said.
Equity producer Total SA has the next Cusiana cargo loading at the end of June to early July.

Current Cusiana production of around 180,000 barrels per day (bpd) is slated to increase to 500,000 bpd by the end of 1997. Loadings are expected to begin rising in the third quarter, trade sources said.
Elsewhere in Latin America, state Petroleos de Venezuela was heard offering sour Mesa-30 at a sharply stronger $2.50 a barrel under WTI/Cushing, while bids were around $3.00 discount, traders said.

The closely guarded grade was last sold around $3.40-50 under WTI/Cushing. The recent dramatic uptick in the Venezuelan quote was partly attributed to a lack of availability of competing barrels such as Ecuadoran Oriente until late July or early August.
Sour barrels may also get a lift out of Iraq's last-minute cancellation of two contracts covering 2.2 million barrels of Basrah Light crude under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
The two shipments, a 900,000 barrel cargo due to begin loading Wednesday for Nippon and a 1.3 million barrel tanker due to load in early June for Bayoil, had received U.N. approval only last Friday.
There had been concerns that the contracts would overshoot the $2.14 billion limit on proceeds under the program.
--Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
